problem: The PFS lead has no single view of open claim lines by CARC class and cannot see how many appealable denials have already passed their filing deadline. Denial specialists track deadlines line by line in the workqueue, so the lead cannot tell where deadline risk sits without opening rows.
users: PFS lead (primary reader of the summary; read-only)
Denial specialist (works the appealable denials the overdue count describes; relies on the same deadline rule in the workqueue)
Biller (resubmits CO-16 and CO-4 lines counted in the denial class)
inScope: Count of open lines per CARC class: denial, patient responsibility, informational, mapped from the six-code demo CARC table
Count of appealable denials whose filing deadline (date of service plus 90 days) has passed
Keeping PR-1 lines out of the appealable denial and overdue counts
Keeping OA-23 lines in the informational class and out of the denial counts
A read-only summary with no line actions
Using the same filing-deadline calculation as the denial specialist workqueue so the two views agree
outOfScope: Any line action from the summary: resubmit, appeal, mark appeal-ready, post, write off, reassign
Changing diagnosis codes, modifiers, or CPT/ICD suggestions
Net collection rate or other A/R financial metrics
Inventing meanings or classes for CARC codes outside the demo table
Emitting 837 claims or loading live 835/ERA clearinghouse files

assumptions.text: The summary counts three classes: denial, patient responsibility, and informational, matching the classes in the CARC table.
The PFS lead cannot act on lines from the summary; the summary is read-only.
A line is overdue when its filing deadline, date of service plus 90 days, has passed.

requirements.statement: The summary shows the number of open lines in each CARC class (denial, patient responsibility, informational), assigning each line to a class only through the demo CARC table.
requirements.rationale: Q-1 and pack/patterns/summary.md define the lead summary as counts by these three CARC classes.

requirements.statement: The summary shows the number of open appealable denials whose filing deadline (date of service plus 90 days) has passed.
requirements.rationale: The brief asks for the overdue appealable denial count; Q-3 defines overdue, and pack/glossary.md says timely filing is counted from the date of service.

requirements.statement: PR-1 lines are counted only under patient responsibility, and OA-23 lines only under informational; neither is included in the appealable denial count or the overdue count.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/summary.md says patient responsibility is not added to the appealable denial count; pack/claim-states.md says PR-1 does not enter denied for appeal and OA-23 is not worked as a denial.

requirements.statement: The summary is read-only: it offers the PFS lead no control that changes a line, claim state, or packet.
requirements.rationale: Q-2 makes the summary read-only, and pack/roles.md says the PFS lead sees counts by CARC class and does not mark packets ready.

requirements.statement: Lines whose CARC is not in the demo table stay unmapped and are never assigned to a class or given a meaning.
requirements.rationale: pack/carc-demo.md says an unknown code stays unmapped and the product must not invent a meaning.

requirements.statement: The overdue count uses the same filing-deadline calculation as the days-remaining value in the denial specialist workqueue, so a line overdue in the summary shows a passed deadline in the workqueue.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/workqueue.md sorts appealable denials by days remaining to the filing deadline; if the two views disagree, the lead and the specialists act on different numbers.

requirements.statement: The summary and its seed data show only synthetic identifiers shaped PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-###.
requirements.rationale: pack/phi-policy.md allows only these identifiers and blocks runs that contain PHI-shaped data.

screens.title: Lead summary
screens.purpose: Read-only tiles showing open-line counts for denial, patient responsibility, and informational, plus the overdue appealable denial count. No action controls.

screens.title: Overdue denial breakdown
screens.purpose: Read-only panel on the summary splitting the overdue appealable denial count by denial code (CO-16, CO-50, CO-197, CO-4), so the lead can see which kind of denial work is behind schedule.

screens.title: Denial specialist workqueue
screens.purpose: Dense table of appealable denials sorted by days remaining to the filing deadline, with patient responsibility in a separate group. Used to confirm it agrees with the summary's overdue count.

openQuestions.text: Proposed: 'appealable denials' for the overdue count means all open lines in the denial class (CO-16, CO-50, CO-197, CO-4), including lines whose next action is resubmission rather than a formal appeal. Needs sign-off.

Proposed: an open line is one whose claim is in denied, appeal-ready, or appeal-submitted, or that carries a PR-1 or OA-23 line not yet closed; paid, closed, upheld, and overturned lines are not counted. Needs sign-off.
Proposed: the deadline has 'passed' when today is later than date of service plus 90 calendar days, so a line on its deadline day is not yet overdue. Needs sign-off.
Proposed: lines with unmapped CARCs are shown as a separate 'unmapped' count outside the three classes so they are not hidden. Needs sign-off.
Proposed: the overdue breakdown by denial code (SCR-2) is read-only and does not link into the workqueue. Needs sign-off.
Open: Should appeal-submitted lines count as overdue once the deadline passes, or does submission before the deadline remove them from the overdue count?
Open: Does the 90-day filing window vary by payer, or does it apply to every payer in this demo?
